children: U.S. Treasury yields pushed higher Thursday morning after the latest wholesale inflation report left markets pricing a firmer path for rates.
The rate-sensitive U.S. 2 Year Treasury yield
climbed 6 basis points to 4.50%, its highest level since July 2024. The benchmark U.S. 10 Year Treasury yield
also rose 5 basis points to 4.90%, a high not seen since November 2023. Further out the curve, the U.S. 30 Year Treasury yield
advanced 5 basis points to 5.34%, matching levels last recorded in June 2007 and marking a 19-year high for the long bond.
The move followed the Bureau of Labor Statistics’ August

. Final-demand prices rose +0.4% month over month, matching estimates. Core PPI, which excludes food and energy, increased by +0.2%, a tenth of a point below the +0.3% consensus. Headline producer prices were up +5.4% from a year earlier.

The combination—an in-line headline print with still-elevated annual inflation—was enough to lift yields across the curve and weigh on equities. Traders treated the data as confirmation that wholesale price pressures have not faded enough to ease concerns about the Federal Reserve’s policy outlook, even as the core reading came in slightly softer than expected.
